description: Create, open, script and archive Vivado projects and everything inside them. Covers Project Mode projects and filesets, the Non-Project (batch) Mode file readers, design checkpoints, part and board selection, and the synthesis/implementation run objects that a headless `vivado -mode batch -source build.tcl` script drives end to end.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Creates a new Vivado project on disk (an .xpr file plus <name>.srcs, .runs and .cache directories) and makes it the current project. This is the entry point of Project Mode, where Vivado manages filesets, compile order, IP and runs for you. Passing -in_memory creates a project that exists only in RAM, which is how Non-Project batch scripts get a part and project context without writing any project files to disk.

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Project name; the file created is <dir>/<name>/<name>.xpr.

parameters.name: <dir>
parameters.description: Parent directory for the project. Defaults to the current working directory.

parameters.name: -part
parameters.description: Target device, e.g. xc7z020clg400-1. Omit it and set the board_part property instead when you target a known board.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing project of the same name instead of erroring.

parameters.name: -in_memory
parameters.description: Create the project only in memory; nothing is written to disk. Used to give a Non-Project script a part context.

parameters.name: -ip
parameters.description: Create a project intended for managing IP (an IP-only 'Manage IP' project).

tools.example:
create_project fir_demo D:/work/fir_demo -part xc7z020clg400-1 -force
set_property target_language Verilog [current_project]
set_property default_lib work [current_project]
puts "Project dir: [get_property DIRECTORY [current_project]]"
tools.notes: In Non-Project (batch) Mode you skip create_project entirely and use set_part plus read_verilog/read_vhdl/read_xdc and synth_design; nothing is managed for you and nothing persists after the session. `create_project -in_memory -part <part>` is the middle ground when a command needs a project object but you do not want files on disk.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Opens an existing Vivado project file (.xpr) and makes it current, restoring its filesets, properties and run definitions. Only one project can be open per Vivado session, so close_project first if another one is open. Use -read_only when a script only needs to report on a project and must not modify it.

parameters.name: <file.xpr>
parameters.description: Path to the project file. Forward slashes work on Windows and are safer in Tcl.

parameters.name: -read_only
parameters.description: Open without taking a write lock; property and source changes cannot be saved.

parameters.name: -part
parameters.description: Open the project against a different part than the one stored in the .xpr.

tools.example:
open_project D:/work/fir_demo/fir_demo.xpr
puts "Part : [get_property PART [current_project]]"
puts "Runs : [get_runs]"
puts "Top  : [get_property TOP [get_filesets sources_1]]"
tools.notes: Opening a project created by an older release migrates it in place, so work on a copy if the original must stay usable by the old version. A stale .xpr.lock directory from a crashed session blocks the open; remove it manually.

tools.name: close_project
tools.description: Closes the current project, discards the in-memory design and releases the project's write lock. Property and source changes are written into the .xpr as they are made, so there is no separate save step. The -delete option additionally removes the project directory from disk, which is convenient for throw-away scripted builds.

parameters.name: -delete
parameters.description: Close the project and delete its directory and files from disk.

tools.example:
open_project D:/work/fir_demo/fir_demo.xpr
report_compile_order -fileset sources_1 -sources
close_project
# In a batch script, finish with:
# exit
tools.notes: close_project also closes any design opened by open_run or open_checkpoint; close_design closes only the design and leaves the project open. A `vivado -mode batch` script should end with `exit` so the process terminates.

tools.name: save_project_as
tools.description: Saves the currently open project under a new name and directory and makes the copy the current project. Use it to branch a project before an experiment, or to produce a clean deliverable copy without run artefacts. By default run results are copied too, which can make the copy very large; -exclude_run_results skips them.

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Name of the new project.

parameters.name: <dir>
parameters.description: Parent directory for the new project.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing project with that name.

parameters.name: -exclude_run_results
parameters.description: Do not copy synthesis/implementation run output into the new project.

parameters.name: -include_local_ip_cache
parameters.description: Copy the project's local out-of-context IP cache as well.

parameters.name: -scan_for_includes
parameters.description: Scan the sources for Verilog include files and add them to the new project.

tools.example:
open_project D:/work/fir_demo/fir_demo.xpr
save_project_as fir_demo_explore D:/work/experiments -force -exclude_run_results
puts "Now working in: [current_project]"
set_property strategy Performance_Explore [get_runs impl_1]
tools.notes: The original project is closed and the copy becomes current. For a single compressed, self-contained file use archive_project; for a text, version-controllable representation use write_project_tcl.

tools.name: current_project
tools.description: Returns the project object for the currently open project, and with an argument makes a different open project current. Nearly every project-scope setting is read or written by passing this object to get_property/set_property, so `[current_project]` is one of the most common idioms in Vivado scripts. It errors if no project is open, which makes it a useful guard in batch flows.

parameters.name: <project>
parameters.description: Optional project object to make current.

tools.example:
set_property board_part xilinx.com:zcu104:part0:1.1 [current_project]
set_property target_language VHDL [current_project]
set_property simulator_language Mixed [current_project]
puts "Name : [current_project]"
puts "Part : [get_property PART [current_project]]"
puts "Dir  : [get_property DIRECTORY [current_project]]"
tools.notes: Useful project properties: PART, BOARD_PART, TARGET_LANGUAGE, DEFAULT_LIB, SIMULATOR_LANGUAGE, SOURCE_MGMT_MODE, DIRECTORY, NAME. Run `list_property [current_project]` to see all of them for your release.

tools.name: archive_project
tools.description: Packs the current project (sources, constraints, IP, block designs and optionally run results) into a single .xpr.zip archive for hand-off or a support case. Sources referenced from outside the project directory are copied in, so the archive opens standalone on another machine. Use it when someone else must reproduce your exact project.

parameters.name: <file.xpr.zip>
parameters.description: Output archive path. Defaults to <project_name>.xpr.zip in the current directory.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing archive file.

parameters.name: -temp_dir
parameters.description: Scratch directory used while staging the archive; point it at a fast local disk for large projects.

parameters.name: -include_run_results
parameters.description: Include synthesis and implementation run output (checkpoints, reports, bitstreams). Greatly increases size.

parameters.name: -include_config_settings
parameters.description: Include the Vivado configuration settings in effect for the project.

parameters.name: -include_local_ip_cache
parameters.description: Include the project's local out-of-context IP cache.

tools.example:
open_project D:/work/fir_demo/fir_demo.xpr
archive_project -force -include_run_results -include_config_settings D:/deliver/fir_demo_v1.xpr.zip
close_project
tools.notes: Leave run results out unless the recipient must inspect the exact implementation output. Unzip the archive and open the .xpr inside it with open_project. For a small, diff-friendly alternative that regenerates the project from your own sources, use write_project_tcl.

tools.name: write_project_tcl
tools.description: Writes a Tcl script that recreates the currently open project: part and board, filesets, source and constraint files, non-default properties, IP, block designs and run definitions. Sourcing that script in a fresh Vivado rebuilds an equivalent project, which is the standard way to keep a Vivado project under version control without committing the .xpr and the generated .runs/.cache directories. Combine -no_copy_sources with -paths_relative_to so the script references the sources in your repository instead of copying them.

parameters.name: <file.tcl>
parameters.description: Path of the Tcl script to write.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing script file.

parameters.name: -no_copy_sources
parameters.description: Reference the sources where they live instead of copying them into the regenerated project. Essential for a repo-based flow.

parameters.name: -paths_relative_to
parameters.description: Base directory that file paths are written relative to, so the script is portable across checkouts.

parameters.name: -target_proj_dir
parameters.description: Directory where the regenerated project will be created when the script runs.

parameters.name: -all_properties
parameters.description: Write every property rather than only the ones that differ from the defaults.

parameters.name: -absolute_path
parameters.description: Write absolute file paths instead of relative ones.

tools.example:
open_project D:/work/fir_demo/fir_demo.xpr
write_project_tcl -force -no_copy_sources -paths_relative_to D:/work/repo D:/work/repo/scripts/create_project.tcl
close_project
# On a clean checkout, rebuild the project headlessly:
#   vivado -mode batch -source scripts/create_project.tcl
tools.notes: The generated script defines an `origin_dir` variable near the top that you can override before sourcing to relocate all relative paths. Run results are never regenerated, so relaunch the runs after rebuilding. Check the generated script into version control together with the RTL, XDC and .xci files.

tools.name: set_part
tools.description: Sets the target device for the current in-memory design or in-memory project. It is the Non-Project Mode counterpart of the -part option of create_project: call it before read_verilog/read_vhdl and synth_design so the tools know the device, package and speed grade. In Project Mode, change the device by setting the PART property on the project object instead.

parameters.name: <part>
parameters.description: Full part name including package and speed grade, e.g. xcvu9p-flga2104-2L-e or xc7a35tcpg236-1.

tools.example:
# Non-Project (batch) flow
set_part xcku040-ffva1156-2-e
read_verilog [glob ./rtl/*.v]
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
synth_design -top top
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_synth.dcp
tools.notes: In Project Mode use `set_property part xc7z020clg400-1 [current_project]`, which also revalidates the IP and marks the runs as needing refresh. get_parts lists every installed part string.

tools.name: get_parts
tools.description: Returns the device parts installed with this Vivado release as part objects carrying properties such as family, device, package and speed grade. Use it to discover the exact part string required by create_project or set_part, and to check that the device family you need was installed. Patterns accept Tcl globs, so `get_parts xc7a*` narrows to a family quickly.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Glob patterns matched against the part name, e.g. xc7z020* or xcku040*.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Property expression, e.g. {SPEED == -2}. Use list_property on a part to see available property names for your release.

parameters.name: -regexp
parameters.description: Treat the patterns as regular expressions.

parameters.name: -nocase
parameters.description: Case-insensitive matching (use with -regexp).

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Return the part(s) associated with other objects, such as a board part.

tools.example:
puts "Installed parts: [llength [get_parts]]"
set p [lindex [get_parts xc7z020clg400-1] 0]
puts [list_property $p]
puts "Speed grade: [get_property SPEED $p]"
foreach part [lsort [get_parts xc7a*]] { puts $part }
tools.notes: Only parts belonging to device families selected during installation are returned, so a missing part usually means a missing family, not a wrong name. get_board_parts is the equivalent for board definitions.

tools.name: get_board_parts
tools.description: Lists the board definitions available from the installed board repositories, returned as vendor:board:part:version strings such as xilinx.com:zcu104:part0:1.1. Setting the project's BOARD_PART property to one of these enables board-aware IP configuration, the Board tab in IP Integrator and the board's pin-out constraints. Use -latest_file_version so a script does not pin itself to an outdated board revision.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Glob patterns matched against the board part name, e.g. *zcu104* or xilinx.com:kc705*.

parameters.name: -latest_file_version
parameters.description: Return only the newest version of each matching board part.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Property expression to narrow the result.

parameters.name: -regexp
parameters.description: Treat the patterns as regular expressions.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Return the board parts associated with other objects, such as a board.

tools.example:
puts [get_board_parts -latest_file_version *zcu104*]
set_property board_part xilinx.com:zcu104:part0:1.1 [current_project]
puts "Part now: [get_property PART [current_project]]"
tools.notes: Setting board_part also sets the project's PART, so on a known board set the board part rather than the part. Board objects themselves are returned by get_boards. Add a custom or vendor board repository with `set_param board.repoPaths {D:/boards}` before opening the project.

tools.name: add_files
tools.description: Adds existing files to a project fileset by reference, so the project stores a pointer to the file where it already lives and edits in your repository are picked up directly. It handles RTL, constraints, IP (.xci), block designs, netlists and simulation sources; a directory argument is added recursively unless -norecurse is given. Use -fileset to target something other than the active sources fileset, for example `-fileset sim_1` for testbenches or `-fileset constrs_1` for XDC.

parameters.name: <files_or_dirs>
parameters.description: One or more file or directory paths; Tcl globbing works, e.g. [glob ./rtl/*.sv].

parameters.name: -fileset
parameters.description: Target fileset: sources_1 for design sources, constrs_1 for constraints, sim_1 for simulation. Defaults to the active sources fileset.

parameters.name: -norecurse
parameters.description: Do not descend into subdirectories when a directory is given.

parameters.name: -scan_for_includes
parameters.description: Scan the added sources for Verilog include files and add those as well.

parameters.name: -copy_to
parameters.description: Copy the files into the given directory first and add the copies.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Add or overwrite even when the file is already present in the fileset.

tools.example:
add_files -fileset sources_1 [glob D:/work/repo/rtl/*.sv]
add_files -fileset sources_1 D:/work/repo/ip/clk_wiz_0/clk_wiz_0.xci
add_files -fileset constrs_1 D:/work/repo/xdc/top.xdc
add_files -fileset sim_1 -norecurse D:/work/repo/sim/tb_top.sv
set_property top fir_top [get_filesets sources_1]
set_property top tb_top  [get_filesets sim_1]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
update_compile_order -fileset sim_1
tools.notes: add_files references files in place; import_files copies them into the project's .srcs directory. Always follow a batch of adds with update_compile_order for each affected fileset, otherwise the compile order and auto-detected top can be stale. In Non-Project Mode use read_verilog/read_vhdl/read_xdc instead.

tools.name: import_files
tools.description: Copies files into the project's <project>.srcs directory and adds the copies to a fileset, making the project self-contained and independent of the original locations. This is what the IDE's 'Copy sources into project' option does. Use it for deliverables and frozen snapshots; prefer add_files when the sources live in version control and must stay there.

parameters.name: <files_or_dirs>
parameters.description: Files or directories to copy into the project.

parameters.name: -fileset
parameters.description: Destination fileset (sources_1, constrs_1, sim_1, or a custom set).

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite copies that already exist in the project.

parameters.name: -norecurse
parameters.description: Do not descend into subdirectories of a directory argument.

parameters.name: -flat
parameters.description: Copy every file into the fileset root instead of recreating the source directory hierarchy.

parameters.name: -relative_to
parameters.description: Base directory used to compute the directory structure that is recreated inside the project.

tools.example:
create_project golden D:/work/golden -part xc7a35tcpg236-1 -force
import_files -fileset sources_1 -flat D:/vendor/release_v2/rtl
import_files -fileset constrs_1 D:/vendor/release_v2/xdc/top.xdc
set_property top top [get_filesets sources_1]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
tools.notes: After importing you are editing the project's copy, so later changes to the original files are ignored. import_ip is the IP-specific equivalent for .xci files and also creates the IP's out-of-context run.

tools.name: remove_files
tools.description: Removes files from a project fileset. The file on disk is not deleted; only the project's reference to it goes away, and for imported files the copy inside the project directory remains until you delete it yourself. Pass file objects returned by get_files so you remove exactly what you matched rather than relying on name matching.

parameters.name: <files>
parameters.description: File names or file objects from get_files.

parameters.name: -fileset
parameters.description: Fileset to remove them from. Defaults to the active sources fileset.

tools.example:
remove_files [get_files -of_objects [get_filesets sources_1] old_top.v]
remove_files -fileset sim_1 [get_files tb_legacy.sv]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
puts [get_files -of_objects [get_filesets sources_1]]
tools.notes: Removing the file that defines the fileset's TOP leaves the project without a valid top module; set a new one with `set_property top <module> [get_filesets sources_1]`. Use Tcl's `file delete` afterwards if the copy on disk should go too.

tools.name: get_files
tools.description: Returns file objects from the project, optionally scoped to a fileset, IP or block design and filtered by property. With -compile_order and -used_in it returns the files in the exact order the compiler will read them, which is the reliable way to confirm what will actually be synthesized or simulated. The objects it returns are what you pass to set_property, remove_files and reporting scripts.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Name patterns such as *.xdc or top.v, matched against the file name.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Restrict to files belonging to a fileset, an IP from get_ips, or a block design.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Property expression, e.g. {FILE_TYPE == "VHDL"} or {IS_ENABLED}.

parameters.name: -compile_order
parameters.description: Return files in processing order: 'sources' for HDL, 'constraints' for XDC. Use together with -used_in.

parameters.name: -used_in
parameters.description: Restrict to files used in synthesis, simulation or implementation.

parameters.name: -all
parameters.description: Also return files inside IP and other sub-designs that are normally hidden.

tools.notes: -compile_order and -used_in are used together; run update_compile_order first or the order may be stale. With no arguments get_files returns every file in the project, including generated IP output products, which is rarely what you want.

tools.name: update_compile_order
tools.description: Re-analyzes the sources in a fileset, re-elaborates the hierarchy and recomputes both the compile order and the automatically detected top module. Run it after any batch of add_files, import_files or remove_files calls, otherwise synthesis and simulation may use a stale order or the wrong top. The IDE does this automatically in the background; a script must call it explicitly.

parameters.name: -fileset
parameters.description: Fileset to update, e.g. sources_1 or sim_1. Defaults to the active sources fileset; call it once per fileset you changed.

tools.example:
add_files -fileset sources_1 [glob ./rtl/*.v]
add_files -fileset sim_1 [glob ./sim/*.v]
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
update_compile_order -fileset sim_1
puts "Auto-detected top: [get_property TOP [get_filesets sources_1]]"
tools.notes: Setting the project's SOURCE_MGMT_MODE property to None disables automatic hierarchy management, after which you must set the top and maintain the order yourself. report_compile_order or `get_files -compile_order sources -used_in synthesis` shows the result.

tools.name: report_compile_order
tools.description: Prints the order in which the source or constraint files of a fileset will be processed, including the library each HDL file is compiled into. The -missing_instances form lists instantiated modules for which no source file was found, which is the fastest way to diagnose an unintended black box. Use it to confirm that update_compile_order produced what you expect before launching a run.

parameters.name: -fileset
parameters.description: Fileset to report on. Defaults to the active sources fileset.

parameters.name: -sources
parameters.description: Report the HDL source compile order.

parameters.name: -constraints
parameters.description: Report the constraint file processing order.

parameters.name: -used_in
parameters.description: Report the order as seen by synthesis, simulation or implementation.

parameters.name: -missing_instances
parameters.description: List instantiated modules with no matching source file (black boxes).

parameters.name: -file
parameters.description: Write the report to a file instead of the console.

parameters.name: -return_string
parameters.description: Return the report as a Tcl string for further processing.

tools.example:
update_compile_order -fileset sources_1
report_compile_order -fileset sources_1 -sources -used_in synthesis
report_compile_order -missing_instances
report_compile_order -fileset constrs_1 -constraints -file D:/work/reports/constraint_order.txt
tools.notes: Constraint order matters: later XDC files override earlier ones, and files whose USED_IN_SYNTHESIS property is false are skipped during synthesis. get_files -compile_order returns the same information as a plain Tcl list for scripting.

tools.name: read_verilog
tools.description: Reads Verilog or SystemVerilog source into the in-memory design without adding it to any project. This is the Non-Project (batch) Mode way to bring in RTL: nothing is copied, no fileset is created and no compile order is managed, so you control the read order yourself. Use -sv to force SystemVerilog parsing for files that do not carry an .sv extension.

parameters.name: <files>
parameters.description: One or more Verilog/SystemVerilog files; read in the order given.

parameters.name: -sv
parameters.description: Parse the files as SystemVerilog regardless of extension.

parameters.name: -library
parameters.description: Compile the files into the named library instead of the default work library.

tools.example:
set_part xcku040-ffva1156-2-e
read_verilog -sv [glob ./rtl/*.sv]
read_verilog ./rtl/legacy/uart.v
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
synth_design -top top
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_synth.dcp
tools.notes: In Project Mode use add_files instead: read_verilog does not register the file with the project, so the source is lost when the design is closed. Read packages and definitions before the modules that use them, since there is no automatic ordering.

tools.name: read_vhdl
tools.description: Reads VHDL source into the in-memory design in Non-Project (batch) Mode. Because VHDL is order- and library-sensitive, you must read packages and entities before the units that reference them and place each file into the correct library with -library. VHDL-2008 constructs are not enabled by default, so pass -vhdl2008 for files that need them.

parameters.name: <files>
parameters.description: One or more VHDL files, read in the order given.

parameters.name: -library
parameters.description: Compile the files into the named VHDL library instead of work.

parameters.name: -vhdl2008
parameters.description: Parse the files using the VHDL-2008 language standard.

tools.example:
set_part xc7a200tsbg484-1
read_vhdl -library common [glob ./rtl/common/*.vhd]
read_vhdl -vhdl2008 ./rtl/axi_stream_pkg.vhd
read_vhdl ./rtl/top.vhd
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
synth_design -top top
tools.notes: In Project Mode the equivalent is add_files plus `set_property file_type {VHDL 2008} [get_files <file>]` and `set_property library common [get_files <file>]`. Mixing libraries requires the referencing file to contain the matching `library`/`use` clauses.

tools.name: read_xdc
tools.description: Reads Xilinx Design Constraints (XDC/SDC) into the in-memory design in Non-Project Mode. Constraints are applied in the order the files are read and later constraints override earlier ones, so read the pin-out and clock definitions before any timing exceptions. -cells and -ref scope the constraints to a specific instance or module, which is how out-of-context constraints for an IP or a module are applied.

parameters.name: <files>
parameters.description: One or more .xdc or .sdc files, applied in the order given.

parameters.name: -cells
parameters.description: Scope the constraints to the given cell instances rather than the whole design.

parameters.name: -ref
parameters.description: Scope the constraints to every instance of the named module or IP reference.

parameters.name: -mode
parameters.description: 'out_of_context' marks the constraints as applying to an out-of-context synthesis of the scoped module.

parameters.name: -unmanaged
parameters.description: Read the file as an unmanaged Tcl script instead of a managed XDC constraints file.

tools.example:
set_part xc7z020clg400-1
read_verilog [glob ./rtl/*.v]
read_xdc ./xdc/pinout.xdc
read_xdc ./xdc/clocks.xdc
read_xdc ./xdc/exceptions.xdc
read_xdc -ref fifo_gen_0 -mode out_of_context ./xdc/fifo_ooc.xdc
synth_design -top top
tools.notes: In Project Mode add constraints with `add_files -fileset constrs_1` and control when each file applies through the USED_IN_SYNTHESIS and USED_IN_IMPLEMENTATION properties. write_xdc exports the constraints currently held in memory.

tools.name: read_ip
tools.description: Reads an existing IP customization file (.xci) into the in-memory design in Non-Project Mode so the IP can be used by the rest of the design. It does not generate the IP: you still call generate_target and synth_ip to produce the output products and the synthesized checkpoint. Use it in batch scripts that build from checked-in .xci files rather than from a project.

parameters.name: <xci_files>
parameters.description: One or more .xci IP customization files.

tools.example:
set_part xc7z020clg400-1
read_ip ./ip/clk_wiz_0/clk_wiz_0.xci
generate_target all [get_ips clk_wiz_0]
synth_ip [get_ips clk_wiz_0]
read_verilog [glob ./rtl/*.v]
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
synth_design -top top
tools.notes: In Project Mode use add_files or import_ip with the .xci, which also registers the IP with the project and creates its out-of-context run. Run `upgrade_ip [get_ips]` when moving an .xci to a newer Vivado release, otherwise generation can fail with a version mismatch.

tools.name: read_edif
tools.description: Reads an EDIF or NGC gate-level netlist into the in-memory design, for third-party synthesis output or encrypted vendor cores that must not be re-synthesized. The netlist stays staged until link_design (or opt_design in a project flow) resolves it against the RTL, filling any matching black box. Use it for mixed flows where part of the design arrives pre-synthesized.

parameters.name: <edif_or_ngc_files>
parameters.description: One or more .edf, .edn or .ngc netlist files.

tools.example:
set_part xc7k325tffg900-2
read_edif ./netlist/vendor_core.edf
read_verilog [glob ./rtl/*.v]
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
synth_design -top top
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_synth.dcp
tools.notes: The module instantiated as a black box in the RTL is filled by the matching EDIF cell during linking, so the cell name must match the instantiated module name exactly. In Project Mode add the .edf/.edn with add_files, which sets its file type to EDIF automatically.

tools.name: read_checkpoint
tools.description: Reads a design checkpoint (.dcp) into memory without opening it as the current design; it stages a netlist that link_design then elaborates and links. Its two main uses are pulling an out-of-context module checkpoint into a black box with -cell, and setting a reference checkpoint for incremental implementation with -incremental. To simply open a complete checkpoint and work on it, use open_checkpoint instead.

parameters.name: <file.dcp>
parameters.description: Path to the design checkpoint to read.

parameters.name: -cell
parameters.description: Black-box instance the checkpoint's netlist is read into, for bottom-up assembly of out-of-context modules.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Name given to the design that will be created from the checkpoint.

parameters.name: -incremental
parameters.description: Use this checkpoint as the reference for incremental implementation rather than loading it as the design.

tools.example:
# Bottom-up assembly of an out-of-context module
set_part xc7k325tffg900-2
read_checkpoint ./checkpoints/top_synth.dcp
read_checkpoint -cell u_dsp_core ./checkpoints/dsp_core_synth.dcp
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
link_design -top top
opt_design
place_design
route_design
tools.notes: read_checkpoint only stages the netlist; no design is current until link_design runs. open_checkpoint is effectively read_checkpoint plus link_design in one step and is what you want for a single, complete checkpoint.

tools.name: get_filesets
tools.description: Returns the project's fileset objects. Every Vivado project has at least sources_1 (design sources), constrs_1 (constraints) and sim_1 (simulation); IP and block designs add their own block filesets. Fileset objects are what you pass as -fileset arguments elsewhere and, importantly, they own the TOP property rather than the project doing so.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Glob patterns matched against fileset names, e.g. sim_* or constrs_1.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Property expression, e.g. {FILESET_TYPE == SimulationSrcs}.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Return the filesets associated with another object, such as an IP or block design.

parameters.name: -regexp
parameters.description: Treat the patterns as regular expressions.

tools.notes: FILESET_TYPE is DesignSrcs, Constrs, SimulationSrcs or BlockSrcs. current_fileset returns the active source, constraint or simulation set. The TOP property belongs to the fileset, so a project can have a different top for synthesis and for simulation.

tools.name: create_fileset
tools.description: Creates a new fileset in the project: a design source set by default, a constraint set with -constrset, a simulation set with -simset, or a block fileset with -blockset. Multiple simulation sets let you keep separate testbench groups (unit tests versus a system testbench) and switch between them, and multiple constraint sets let you build the same RTL for different boards. After creating one, populate it with add_files and make it active with current_fileset or a run's CONSTRSET property.

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Name of the new fileset.

parameters.name: -simset
parameters.description: Create a simulation fileset (holds testbenches and their own TOP).

parameters.name: -constrset
parameters.description: Create a constraint fileset (holds XDC files).

parameters.name: -blockset
parameters.description: Create a block fileset, used for block design sources.

parameters.name: -clone_simset
parameters.description: Populate the new simulation set with a copy of an existing one.

tools.example:
# A second simulation set for unit tests
create_fileset -simset sim_unit
add_files -fileset sim_unit [glob D:/work/repo/sim/unit/*.sv]
set_property top tb_fir_unit [get_filesets sim_unit]
update_compile_order -fileset sim_unit
current_fileset -simset [get_filesets sim_unit]
launch_simulation

# A second constraint set for a different board
create_fileset -constrset constrs_zcu104
add_files -fileset constrs_zcu104 D:/work/repo/xdc/zcu104.xdc
set_property constrset constrs_zcu104 [get_runs impl_1]
tools.notes: A run selects its constraints through the CONSTRSET property; only one simulation set is active at a time and current_fileset -simset selects it. Remove an unused set with delete_fileset.

tools.name: delete_fileset
tools.description: Deletes a fileset from the project together with its list of file references; the files themselves remain on disk. Use it to clean up experimental constraint or simulation sets after a sweep. The fileset must not be in use, so switch the active simulation set and reassign any run that points at the constraint set first.

parameters.name: <fileset>
parameters.description: Fileset name or object from get_filesets.

tools.example:
current_fileset -simset [get_filesets sim_1]
delete_fileset [get_filesets sim_unit]
set_property constrset constrs_1 [get_runs impl_1]
delete_fileset [get_filesets constrs_zcu104]
puts [get_filesets]
tools.notes: Vivado refuses to delete the active source fileset or a constraint set still referenced by a run; change the run's CONSTRSET property or delete the run with delete_runs first. Deleting a fileset never deletes source files from disk.

tools.name: set_property
tools.description: Sets a property on any Vivado object: project, fileset, file, run, IP, cell, port or net. It is the single mechanism behind almost all project configuration, because the top module lives on the fileset, the language and library live on the file, the strategy and constraint set live on the run, and the part and board live on the project. Use the -dict form to set several properties on the same object in one call.

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Property name; case-insensitive, e.g. top, file_type, library, used_in_synthesis, part, board_part, strategy.

parameters.name: <value>
parameters.description: Value to assign. Brace values that contain spaces, e.g. {VHDL 2008}.

parameters.name: <objects>
parameters.description: One or more objects, typically [current_project], [get_filesets ...], [get_files ...] or [get_runs ...].

parameters.name: -dict
parameters.description: A {name value name value ...} list applied to the same objects in one call.

tools.example:
# TOP lives on the fileset, not on the project
set_property top fir_top [get_filesets sources_1]
set_property top tb_fir  [get_filesets sim_1]

# File type and library
set_property file_type {VHDL 2008}   [get_files axi_stream_pkg.vhd]
set_property file_type SystemVerilog [get_files fir_top.sv]
set_property library common          [get_files axi_stream_pkg.vhd]

# Where each constraint file is used
set_property used_in_synthesis      false [get_files timing_impl.xdc]
set_property used_in_implementation true  [get_files timing_impl.xdc]
set_property used_in_simulation     false [get_files top_pinout.xdc]

# Several project properties at once
set_property -dict {target_language Verilog default_lib work} [current_project]
set_property board_part xilinx.com:zcu104:part0:1.1 [current_project]
tools.notes: `list_property <object>` shows every valid property for an object and `list_property_value <property> <object>` shows the legal values, which is far safer than guessing. Setting an unknown property is an error; property names are case-insensitive but values often are not.

tools.name: get_property
tools.description: Reads one property from one object and returns its value as a string. It is how a script inspects project state: the current part, a file's type, whether a run finished, or how far a run got before it stopped. Paired with get_runs, get_files and current_project it provides the gating logic that makes a headless build script fail loudly instead of silently producing nothing.

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Property name, e.g. PART, TOP, STATUS, PROGRESS, NEEDS_REFRESH, DIRECTORY, FILE_TYPE.

parameters.name: <object>
parameters.description: A single object; get_property does not accept a list.

parameters.name: -min / -max
parameters.description: For properties that hold a range of values (such as timing corner values), return the minimum or maximum.

tools.example:
puts "Part : [get_property PART [current_project]]"
puts "Top  : [get_property TOP  [get_filesets sources_1]]"

launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run impl_1

set progress [get_property PROGRESS      [get_runs impl_1]]
set status   [get_property STATUS        [get_runs impl_1]]
set stale    [get_property NEEDS_REFRESH [get_runs impl_1]]
puts "impl_1: progress=$progress status=$status needs_refresh=$stale"
if {$progress ne "100%"} {
    error "Implementation did not complete: $status"
}
tools.notes: PROGRESS is a string such as "100%", not a number, so compare it as a string. NEEDS_REFRESH is 1 when sources or properties changed after the run completed, meaning the results are stale. STATUS carries the last step reported, for example "write_bitstream Complete!" or a failure message. Use list_property to discover readable properties.

tools.name: write_checkpoint
tools.description: Writes the current in-memory design (netlist, constraints, and placement and routing if present) to a design checkpoint (.dcp). Checkpoints are the unit of exchange in Non-Project Mode: write one after each stage so any stage can be reloaded later without rerunning the whole flow. -cell writes only the sub-design under a given instance, which is how out-of-context module checkpoints are produced.

parameters.name: <file.dcp>
parameters.description: Output checkpoint path.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing checkpoint file; without it an existing file is an error.

parameters.name: -cell
parameters.description: Write only the design under the given cell instance, producing an out-of-context module checkpoint.

tools.example:
synth_design -top top -part xcku040-ffva1156-2-e
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_synth.dcp
opt_design
place_design
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_place.dcp
route_design
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_route.dcp
report_timing_summary -file ./reports/post_route_timing.rpt
tools.notes: Project Mode runs write their own checkpoints into <project>.runs/<run>/; locate them with `get_property DIRECTORY [get_runs impl_1]`. A checkpoint records the part, so it can be reopened on any machine with the same Vivado release and device family installed.

tools.name: open_checkpoint
tools.description: Opens a design checkpoint as the current in-memory design in one step: it reads the checkpoint and links the design for you, with no project involved. Use it to re-open a post-synthesis or post-route DCP for analysis, to continue implementation from a stage, or to inspect results on a machine that has no project. It is the Non-Project counterpart of open_run.

parameters.name: <file.dcp>
parameters.description: Checkpoint to open.

parameters.name: -part
parameters.description: Override the part stored in the checkpoint.

parameters.name: -ignore_timing
parameters.description: Skip reading the timing constraints, giving a much faster load when only the netlist or placement is needed.

tools.example:
open_checkpoint ./checkpoints/post_route.dcp
report_timing_summary -file ./reports/timing.rpt
report_utilization   -file ./reports/util.rpt
write_bitstream -force ./bit/top.bit
close_design
tools.notes: open_checkpoint closes any design that is already open and does not need a project. Use read_checkpoint plus link_design instead when you must assemble several checkpoints (for example an out-of-context module into a black box) before the design is elaborated.

tools.name: link_design
tools.description: Elaborates the netlists staged in memory by read_checkpoint, read_edif or synthesis into a single linked in-memory design that the implementation commands can operate on. It resolves black boxes against the sub-netlists that were read for them and applies the chosen constraint set. Use it whenever a design is assembled from separate netlist pieces rather than opened from one complete checkpoint.

parameters.name: -top
parameters.description: Top-level module of the linked design.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Name given to the resulting design, useful when several designs are open.

parameters.name: -part
parameters.description: Target part, if not already established by set_part or the checkpoint.

parameters.name: -constrset
parameters.description: Constraint set to apply (Project Mode object).

parameters.name: -mode
parameters.description: 'out_of_context' links the design as a standalone module, so no I/O buffers are inserted.

tools.example:
set_part xc7k325tffg900-2
read_checkpoint ./checkpoints/top_synth.dcp
read_checkpoint -cell u_dsp ./checkpoints/dsp_core_synth.dcp
read_xdc ./xdc/top.xdc
link_design -top top -name assembled
opt_design
place_design
route_design
write_checkpoint -force ./checkpoints/post_route.dcp
tools.notes: In Project Mode, open_run performs the equivalent link on a completed synthesis run. -mode out_of_context is what an out-of-context IP run uses, so the module keeps its ports as internal pins instead of gaining I/O buffers.

tools.name: open_run
tools.description: Opens the results of a completed Project Mode run as the current in-memory design. For a synthesis run it links the netlist; for an implementation run it loads the placed and routed design. Use it after wait_on_run when a script needs to run reports, apply ECOs, probe nets or write a bitstream from a project run.

parameters.name: <run>
parameters.description: Run name or object, e.g. synth_1 or [get_runs impl_1].

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Name for the resulting design, e.g. netlist_1. Helpful when several designs are open at once.

parameters.name: -pr_config
parameters.description: Partial reconfiguration configuration to open for a PR design.

tools.example:
launch_runs synth_1 -jobs 8
wait_on_run synth_1
open_run synth_1 -name netlist_1
report_utilization -file D:/work/reports/synth_util.rpt
close_design

launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run impl_1
open_run impl_1
report_timing_summary -file D:/work/reports/impl_timing.rpt
close_design
tools.notes: The run must have completed; check `get_property PROGRESS [get_runs synth_1]` first or open_run errors. open_checkpoint is the Non-Project equivalent. Use current_design to see what is open and close_design to release it before opening another.

tools.name: current_design
tools.description: Returns the design object currently open in memory, and with an argument switches between several designs opened under different -name values. Scripts use it to confirm that a design is actually open before running analysis commands, and to read design-scope properties such as the part and top module. It raises an error when no design is open, which makes it a convenient guard.

parameters.name: <design>
parameters.description: Optional design object or name to make current.

tools.example:
if {[catch {current_design}]} {
    open_checkpoint ./checkpoints/post_route.dcp
}
puts "Design: [current_design]"
puts "Part  : [get_property PART [current_design]]"
puts "Top   : [get_property TOP  [current_design]]"
report_utilization -file ./reports/util.rpt
tools.notes: Wrap it in `catch` for a safe 'is a design open?' test, since it errors rather than returning an empty string. In Project Mode the open design corresponds to the run opened by open_run, under the name given by -name.

tools.name: close_design
tools.description: Closes the design currently open in memory without closing the project. Use it between stages of a script that opens several runs or checkpoints in turn, so the previous netlist does not stay resident and consume memory. Anything you changed in memory (ECOs, edited constraints) is lost unless it was saved first.
tools.example:
open_run synth_1 -name netlist_1
report_utilization -file ./reports/synth_util.rpt
close_design

open_run impl_1
report_timing_summary -file ./reports/impl_timing.rpt
report_power -file ./reports/power.rpt
close_design
tools.notes: close_project closes any open design as well, so an explicit close_design is only needed when the project stays open. If you edited constraints in memory, call save_constraints (Project Mode) or write_xdc before closing, and write_checkpoint to preserve netlist edits.

tools.name: create_run
tools.description: Defines a new synthesis or implementation run in the project. An implementation run must name its -parent_run (the synthesis run providing the netlist) and a -flow string that matches the installed release, for example {Vivado Implementation 2024}. Creating several runs with different strategies or constraint sets is how you sweep implementation options and compare the results side by side.

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Name of the new run, e.g. impl_explore_1.

parameters.name: -flow
parameters.description: Flow name for the installed release, e.g. {Vivado Synthesis 2024} or {Vivado Implementation 2024}.

parameters.name: -strategy
parameters.description: Named strategy such as Flow_PerfOptimized_high (synthesis) or Performance_ExplorePostRoutePhysOpt (implementation).

parameters.name: -parent_run
parameters.description: For an implementation run, the synthesis run that supplies the netlist.

parameters.name: -constrset
parameters.description: Constraint set the run uses; lets two runs build the same RTL against different XDC.

parameters.name: -part
parameters.description: Target part for this run, if it differs from the project part.

parameters.name: -report_strategy
parameters.description: Named report strategy controlling which reports the run generates automatically.

tools.example:
create_run synth_perf -flow {Vivado Synthesis 2024} -strategy {Flow_PerfOptimized_high} -constrset constrs_1
create_run impl_perf -flow {Vivado Implementation 2024} -parent_run synth_perf -strategy {Performance_ExplorePostRoutePhysOpt} -constrset constrs_1
launch_runs impl_perf -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run impl_perf
puts [get_property STATUS [get_runs impl_perf]]
tools.notes: The -flow and -strategy strings are release-specific and create_run errors on an unknown one. Read the exact strings for your install from an existing run: `get_property FLOW [get_runs synth_1]` and `get_property STRATEGY [get_runs impl_1]`.

tools.name: launch_runs
tools.description: Starts one or more synthesis or implementation runs as background jobs. -jobs controls how much work runs in parallel and -to_step stops the flow at a named step, most commonly write_bitstream so the run produces a bitstream in one call. launch_runs returns immediately, so any batch script must follow it with wait_on_run or the Vivado process will exit while the runs are still going.

parameters.name: <runs>
parameters.description: One or more run names or objects, e.g. `synth_1 impl_1` or [get_runs impl_*].

parameters.name: -jobs
parameters.description: Maximum number of jobs to run in parallel; set it to the number of cores you want to use.

parameters.name: -to_step
parameters.description: Run through this step and stop, e.g. write_bitstream, route_design, opt_design.

parameters.name: -next_step
parameters.description: Advance a partially completed run by one step.

parameters.name: -scripts_only
parameters.description: Generate the run scripts without executing them, for submission to a compute farm.

parameters.name: -dir
parameters.description: Directory in which to create the run directories, instead of <project>.runs.

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Reset and relaunch a run that has already completed.

tools.example:
launch_runs synth_1 -jobs 8
wait_on_run synth_1
if {[get_property PROGRESS [get_runs synth_1]] ne "100%"} {
    error "Synthesis failed: [get_property STATUS [get_runs synth_1]]"
}

launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run impl_1
puts [get_property STATUS [get_runs impl_1]]
tools.notes: Launching an implementation run whose parent synthesis run is out of date makes Vivado rerun synthesis first. You can launch synthesis and implementation in one call (`launch_runs synth_1 impl_1 -jobs 8 -to_step write_bitstream`), but you still need a wait_on_run for each run you depend on. Use -scripts_only plus the generated runme scripts for LSF/SGE submission.

tools.name: wait_on_run
tools.description: Blocks the Tcl interpreter until the named run finishes, fails, or an optional timeout expires. It is mandatory in `vivado -mode batch -source build.tcl` scripts because launch_runs is asynchronous and the script would otherwise reach `exit` while the run is still in progress. After it returns, read the run's PROGRESS and STATUS properties to decide whether the run actually succeeded.

parameters.name: <run>
parameters.description: Run name or object to wait for.

parameters.name: -timeout
parameters.description: Maximum wait in minutes; the command returns when it expires even if the run is still going.

tools.example:
launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run -timeout 120 impl_1

set progress [get_property PROGRESS [get_runs impl_1]]
set status   [get_property STATUS   [get_runs impl_1]]
puts "impl_1: $progress / $status"
if {$progress ne "100%"} {
    puts "FAILED: $status"
    exit 1
}
exit 0
tools.notes: wait_on_run returns normally when a run fails, so never treat a successful return as a successful build; always check PROGRESS afterwards. Newer Vivado releases also provide wait_on_runs, which accepts several runs in a single call.

tools.name: reset_run
tools.description: Resets a run to its not-started state, clearing the results under <project>.runs/<run> so the next launch starts clean. Use it when a run failed, when its inputs changed, or before relaunching with a different strategy or constraint set. -from_step resets an implementation run only from a given step onward, which avoids rerunning the earlier steps.

parameters.name: <run>
parameters.description: Run name or object to reset.

parameters.name: -from_step
parameters.description: Reset the implementation run from this step forward, e.g. place_design or phys_opt_design.

parameters.name: -prev_step
parameters.description: Reset the run back to the previous step.

tools.example:
if {[get_property NEEDS_REFRESH [get_runs impl_1]]} {
    reset_run impl_1
}
reset_run synth_1
launch_runs synth_1 -jobs 8
wait_on_run synth_1

# Redo only placement onwards after a constraint tweak
reset_run impl_1 -from_step place_design
launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run impl_1
tools.notes: Resetting a synthesis run invalidates the implementation runs that name it as -parent_run, which will then rerun synthesis. reset_run keeps the run definition; delete_runs removes it entirely. Newer releases also provide reset_runs for several runs in one call.

tools.name: get_runs
tools.description: Returns the run objects defined in the project: the default synth_1 and impl_1, any runs you created, and the out-of-context runs Vivado creates for IP and block designs. Use it to enumerate runs for a status report, to filter for the ones that went stale, and to supply run objects to launch_runs, reset_run and get_property. Patterns accept Tcl globs such as impl_*.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Glob patterns matched against run names, e.g. impl_* or synth_1.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Property expression, e.g. {IS_IMPLEMENTATION} or {NEEDS_REFRESH}.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Return the runs associated with another object, such as an IP.

parameters.name: -regexp
parameters.description: Treat the patterns as regular expressions.

tools.notes: Useful run properties: PROGRESS, STATUS, NEEDS_REFRESH, IS_SYNTHESIS, IS_IMPLEMENTATION, PARENT, STRATEGY, FLOW, CONSTRSET, PART and DIRECTORY. Filter with {IS_IMPLEMENTATION} to exclude synthesis and out-of-context IP runs.

tools.name: current_run
tools.description: Returns the run that is currently active in the project, and with an argument makes a different run active. A project has one active synthesis run and one active implementation run, selected with -synthesis and -implementation. Scripts use it so they do not have to hard-code the names synth_1 and impl_1 when several runs exist.

parameters.name: -synthesis
parameters.description: Operate on the active synthesis run.

parameters.name: -implementation
parameters.description: Operate on the active implementation run.

parameters.name: <run>
parameters.description: Run to make active; omit to query the current one.

tools.example:
puts "Active synth: [current_run -synthesis]"
puts "Active impl : [current_run -implementation]"

current_run -implementation [get_runs impl_perf]
set r [current_run -implementation]
launch_runs $r -to_step write_bitstream -jobs 8
wait_on_run $r
puts [get_property STATUS $r]
tools.notes: The active run is the one the IDE's Run Synthesis / Run Implementation buttons target. Setting it does not launch anything. Always pass -synthesis or -implementation explicitly so the intent is unambiguous.

tools.name: delete_runs
tools.description: Removes run definitions from the project and, by default, deletes their result directories under <project>.runs. Use it to clean up experiment runs after a strategy sweep, or to drop a run that blocks deletion of a constraint set or a parent synthesis run. Pass -noclean_dir to keep the results on disk while removing the run from the project.

parameters.name: <runs>
parameters.description: One or more run names or objects to delete.

parameters.name: -noclean_dir
parameters.description: Leave the run's directory and its results on disk; only the project's definition is removed.

tools.notes: Deleting a synthesis run also removes the implementation runs that reference it as their parent. When you only want to clear the results and relaunch later, use reset_run instead so the run definition, strategy and constraint set are preserved.
